candidates.why: Line 11733 sets o->color.name = o->color.book_name, so both fields alias the same strdup'd buffer (from line 11729). Then line 11739 tmp = o->color.name and line 11742 free(tmp) frees that buffer, but o->color.book_name is never reassigned in this branch and still points to the freed memory — a dangling pointer left in the struct.

Line 11752 tmp = o->color.book_name; line 11753 reassigns o->color.book_name = bit_utf8_to_TU(o->color.book_name,...) (reads old buffer, returns new); line 11755 free(tmp) frees the old buffer. This is safe only because book_name was reassigned before the free; but the same pattern at 11756-11759 for o->color.name relies on the reassignment ordering — worth flagging as a fragile free-then-use pattern where the freed pointer (tmp) aliases a struct field.

Line 1084 free(o->name) then line 1086 reassigns o->name = bit_utf8_to_TU(...). The free happens before the reassignment; if bit_utf8_to_TU returned NULL (OOM path at bits.c:2581) o->name would be left NULL, and any later use of the old name is gone. Not a classic UAF but a free-then-overwrite of a struct field that other code may still reference.
